newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli defence chief denies Iran rescue rumour.
newsitem.headline: Israeli defence chief denies Iran rescue rumour.

text.p: It would have been the perfect holiday gift for Israelis on the eve of Passover, when Jews celebrate deliverance from captivity in ancient Egypt.

Rumours swept the Jewish state over the weekend that Israeli commandos, in a daring mission in Iran or Lebanon, had rescued Israeli airman Ron Arad, missing and believed captured after being shot down on a mission over Lebanon in 1986.
Untrue, Defence Minister Yitzhak Mordechai said on Sunday.

"I have no idea where this came from," he told Army Radio. "I regret this whole rumour mill. I am sorry to say there is nothing new on Ron Arad...It is just unbelievable how serious and thinking people can get caught up in baseless rumours."

Listeners telephoned radio talks shows to say how their spirits had been lifted by the rumour which spread by word of mouth while Israelis waited to see if Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu would be indicted in a corruption scandal.

"My son has a friend who has a friend in the 'Sayeret Matkal' (commando unit) who said it went into Iran and rescued Arad at the cost of two Israeli dead and six wounded," one woman told Israel Radio.

A legislator said he was telephoned by a friend in a kibbutz who told him that she had been called by a well-known Israeli journalist asking if it was true a soldier from the collective farm had been killed in the mission.
Mordechai was closed-mouth about Arad's whereabouts.
"We don't have precise information. Any place is a possibility," he said.

Israeli officials have said they believe that Iran or Iran-backed guerrillas in Lebanon are holding Arad, a navigator who ejected from a stricken Phantom fighter-bomber. The pilot was rescued within minutes by an Israeli helicopter.
